html:
The Treaty of Gulistan, signed on 24 October 1813 in Karabakh, ended a war between Russia and Qajar Iran and gave Russia most of the khanates of today's Azerbaijan. Iran also gave up Dagestan and its claims to eastern Georgia.

Iran lost Baku, Shirvan, Karabakh, Ganja and other khanates and the right to keep a navy on the Caspian. A second war ended with the Treaty of Turkmenchay in 1828, which added the khanates of Erivan and Nakhchivan and fixed the border on the Aras River. The two treaties divided the Azerbaijani speaking people: those north of the Aras came under the Russian Empire, while a larger number stayed in Iran, where they still live today.
